To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The residues of insecticides and acardiacides were found in 94.4% of beeswax samples.

1) beeswax contamination was found to be widespread in French apiaries, 2) the main compounds found in beeswax were tau fluvalinate, pyrethroids and coumaphos, 3) the main source of contamination was the use of acaricides, 4) the contamination of beeswax was not related to the geographical origin of apiaries

(a) beeswax contamination was due to in hive acaricides and environmental pollution; (b) the most frequently detected residues were tau fluvalinate, cypermethrin and coumaphos; (c) coumaphos was the compound with the highest mean concentration (792.6 mu g kg(-1)) and (d) the mean concentration of residues was lower in 2003 than in 2002, probably due to the reduction of coumaphos

the monitoring of pesticide residues in beeswaxes collected from honey bee hives.
the development of a new method for the determination of pesticide residues in beeswaxes.
the development of a new analytical method for the simultaneous determination of pesticides residues in beeswaxes.

, at least in France, there is no evidence of any direct link between beeswax residues of insecticides and acari cides and colony losses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coumaphos was the main acaricide residue in beeswax.
beeswax residues were found in 75.4% of the samples, with coumaphos, tau fluvalinate and endosulfans being the most frequently detected.
the use of acaricides and insecticides in apiaries has to be reduced in order to protect honey bees from the risk of intoxication.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of tau fluvalinate, which is the most widely used acaricide in France, should be reconsidered because of its high toxicity to honey bees and its frequent presence at high concentrations in beeswax.
beeswax residues of insecticide and acaricide residues are frequent in French apiaries and are likely to affect honey bee health.
the use of tau fluvalinate and coumaphos in French beekeeping should be reconsidered.
